text:
incidents-bot: Pager — smart-routing alert: sudden 3.8x qps spike in eu-west affecting economy tier (requests queuing; 95p latency > 1.2s). Auto-fallbacks triggered. See dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/smart-routing/eu-west

oncall_eli: taking this — /take incidents (oncall)

sre_maya: digging into routing logs now. preliminary looks like an ad-hoc traffic burst from a handful of orgs hitting long seq lengths.

routing_tim: can we temporarily bias routing towards low-latency pools in eu-west? shift policy from cost->latency for 10m?

eng_runtime_lin: we can push a policy patch. 2 options: (A) global latency bias for eu-west, (B) drop economy-tier to save capacity. Option A cheaper for UX, B gives more headroom.

product_ana: customer-impact: I see ~60 orgs with elevated error-rate; top 5 accounts generate 45% of the surge. CS might need to notify paid customers if we throttle.

cs_jordan: flagged top 5 for outreach. don't route any hard throttles at paid-pro accounts unless ops approves.

oncall_eli: agreed. plan: 1) enable temporary regional latency bias (routing change) 2) soft-rate-limit economy tier (50% throttle) 3) monitor 10m, escalate if errors persist.

routing_tim: prepping the patch. posting config snippet below, will apply as canary to eu-west-1 pool first.

routing_tim: ```
# smart routing patch
{
  "region_policies": {
    "eu-west": {
      "priority_order": ["latency","cost","quota"],
      "tier_overrides": {
        "economy": {"max_qps": "0.5x", "fallback": "standard"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

eng_runtime_lin: applied canary to eu-west-1 (pool-a). monitoring traces. Latency 95p dropped from 1.28s -> 0.42s for canary flows.

incidents-bot: deploy-bot started rollout: routing-patch-2425001234 (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Estimated rollout 8m.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to pool-a (10%).

oncall_eli: good. also start soft-rate-limit on economy tier in eu-west with header-based exception for orgs in paid_tier list. don't throttle paid accounts.

eng_runtime_lin: running command: `redwoodctl traffic-control set --region eu-west --tier economy --qps-multiplier 0.5 --except-paid`

eng_runtime_lin: soft-rate-limit active. verifying metrics.

sre_maya: errors down 78% overall. CPU on pool nodes trending normal. KV cache hit rate unchanged. Looks like we cut the worst congestion.

product_ana: CS wants to send status update to affected customers in 20m if stable. please mark for follow-up.

cs_jordan: noted. drafting message. will wait for green from oncall.

routing_tim: starting automated rollout to 50% now.

deploy-bot: rollout at 50% — monitoring for anomalies.

oncall_eli: check probing traffic (synthetic) across eu-west subnets and ap-south as control. post latency numbers here.

eng_runtime_lin: probe results: eu-west avg p95 0.48s, ap-south control p95 0.52s (unchanged). No regressions.

sre_maya: there is a small spike of 503s from one legacy route; investigating fallback logic.

routing_tim: found mis-configured fallback TTL causing retries to pile. patching to increase backoff and cap retries.

routing_tim: patched fallback backoff: `max_retries=2, base_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=2s`

sre_maya: 503s dropped to baseline. overall system healthy.

noncall_eli: hold full rollout until we confirm paid accounts unaffected. eng_runtime_lin confirm the exception list applied?

eng_runtime_lin: exception list present and validated against billing service. sample paid-org requests show no throttle in headers.

product_ana: recommend keeping economy-tier soft-throttle for 30 more minutes, then gradually relax if stable. prepare rollback steps.

oncall_eli: agreed. schedule: keep policy for 30m, if error-rate < 5% revert multiplier to 0.9, then to 1.0 after 15m.

cs_jordan: sending proactive note to top 5 affected customers now (marked as FYI only).

cs_jordan: message sent: "We're seeing transient capacity pressure in eu-west and applied temporary mitigation to improve latency. No expected impact to paid plans. We're monitoring closely." :email:

incidents-bot: Alert cleared: qps normalized for eu-west after routing rollout and economy-tier soft-limit. Incident duration 00:27:46.

noncall_eli: closing loop — mitigation successful. follow-ups: 1) postmortem with root cause (bursting orgs + fallback retry TTL) 2) add auto-detection for multi-org bursts to trigger preemptive tier-shed 3) audit routing fallback TTL defaults. owners: eng-runtime_lin, routing_tim, sre_maya.

product_ana: creating postmortem doc and linking eval prompt set to check quality regressions from routing change.

sre_maya: adding graphs to the incident timeline.

oncall_eli: thanks everyone. tagging for runbook updates. :thumbsup:

cs_jordan: closing customer loop and follow-up scheduled.

routing_tim: will follow up with change proposal to add regional surge-profiles (auto-lift economy for short bursts).

incidents-bot: thread archived.
